coverage_rationale: The article discusses the use of automated drug review tools in the industry, with Gallagher Bassett providing expert commentary alongside other organizations.

gb_spokespeople.name: Leah Sharp
gb_spokespeople.title: Senior Vice President of GBCare and Managed Care

gb_statements.speaker: Leah Sharp
gb_statements.text: It’s never going to replace the judgment call

gb_statements.speaker: Leah Sharp
gb_statements.text: At Gallagher Bassett Services, pharmacy benefit managers do not automatically decide drug authorizations, said Leah Sharp, Huntsville, Alabama-based senior vice president of GBCare and managed care.

gb_statements.speaker: Leah Sharp
gb_statements.text: Clinical decision-support tools instead give resolution managers and clinical professionals real-time guidance based on state regulations, treatment guidelines, clinical evidence, health-risk scores and client rules, she said.

gb_statements.speaker: Leah Sharp
gb_statements.text: AI is being used to summarize medical records, claim notes and treatment timelines, improving workflow without directing whether a drug should be approved or denied, she said.

key_messages.message: Gallagher Bassett emphasizes the importance of human judgment in drug authorization decisions, even when using automated tools.
key_messages.supporting_excerpt: It’s never going to replace the judgment call

key_messages.message: Gallagher Bassett uses AI to improve workflow by summarizing medical records and claim notes, but not to make drug approval decisions.
key_messages.supporting_excerpt: AI is being used to summarize medical records, claim notes and treatment timelines, improving workflow without directing whether a drug should be approved or denied, she said.

key_messages.message: Gallagher Bassett's clinical decision-support tools provide real-time guidance to professionals based on various regulations and guidelines.
